Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

certain adjective

a particular

also a certain

classical

Cic. Off. 1.104: lūdendī etiam est quīdam modus retinendus
Traupman 86: quōdam diē

quīdam, quaedam, quoddam

pronoun and adjective; quiddam as a noun

a certain, a particular (one not named); some

It also softens a word: timiditāte ingenuā quādam, with a sort of well-bred shyness (Cic. de Or. 2.10).

Other words

  • certus, certa, certum — certain, particular (people, days)

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 64: habet certōs suī studiōsōs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 288

    Lewis & Short: sometimes used like quīdam, of things or people that exist but are not named.

  • sunt quī (+ subjunctive) — certain people, some (who …)

    phrase · also used · classical · Quint. 10.1.93: sunt quī Propertium mālint

Examples

  • lūdendī etiam est quīdam modus retinendus

    even in play a certain limit must be keptCic. Off. 1.104

  • bene quīdam dīxit dē amīcō suō, 'dīmidium animae suae'

    someone put it well, calling his friend “half of his soul”Aug. Conf. 4.6.11

  • Quōdam diē sēcum cōgitāvit

    One day he thought to himselfLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • sunt quī Propertium mālint

    some prefer PropertiusQuint. 10.1.93

See also sure.
